title: India's BitChat Ban: A Test of Decentralized Tech vs State Control
seo_title: BitChat Ban India: Decentralized Mesh Networks and State Con
meta_description: India orders BitChat's removal, citing risks of anonymous coordination. A key test for decentralized tech and state surveillance capabilities.
social_hook: India just banned a decentralized app that works without the internet. This is a direct power play against tech that evades state control. #BitChat #IndiaTech
seo_tags: BitChat, India, Decentralized, Mesh Network, Cybersecurity, Surveillance, IT Act, Jack Dorsey, Censorship Resistance, State Control
key_takeaways: The government's order targets BitChat's ability to facilitate anonymous coordination during protests and internet shutdowns.
BitChat's decentralized architecture, which requires no internet or central servers, is fundamentally at odds with state surveillance models.
The action leverages Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act, raising questions about due process and the future of decentralized tech in India.
This is a strategic move to maintain control over communication channels and prevent the use of censorship-resistant technology for unlawful activities.
